entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking: The wallet logs `IDENTITY_ACCESS_DETECTED` entries to the tamper-evident audit log, but its mapping drops the detection method and confidence, so a guess from the user-agent string is stored as a confirmed event. I'm filing an issue for it.

input.command:
cat > "$TEMP/claude/C--Users-Lenovo--aaCoding-miTch/daedf558-7fd2-4f6c-844d-47f557e35491/scratchpad/issue-audit.md" <<'EOF'
## Finding (observed 2026-11-01 at origin/master `002ce5e`)

The wallet writes **heuristic guesses from a mock service** into the tamper-evident audit log as if they were detected events.

**Path**
1. `src/apps/wallet-pwa/src/services/PrivacyAuditService.ts:63` — `// Mock Service Implementation`. `auditTransaction()` sniffs `navigator.userAgent` and returns hard-coded "trackers" (e.g. Windows → "Windows Telemetry", confidence 85; Android → "OS-level telemetry active", 95). All are `detection.method: 'HEURISTIC'`.
2. `src/apps/wallet-pwa/src/App.tsx:683` — after the user accepts the privacy-audit modal, `recordIdentityFirewallEvents(decision_id, verifier_did, context.detectedTrackers)` is called.
3. `src/apps/wallet-pwa/src/services/WalletService.ts:1853` → `mapTrackingPointToIdentityMetadata` (`:122`) → `auditLog.append('IDENTITY_ACCESS_DETECTED', …)`.

**Problem**
- The mapping keeps `actor_label`, `severity`, `persistence`, `linkability`, `source: 'privacy_audit_service'`, but **drops `detection.method` and `confidence`**. A reader of the audit log (or the DataFlow / consent-manager views that consume it) cannot tell a UA-string guess from an observed access.
- The audit log is meant to be evidence. Entries derived from a mock with fixed confidence numbers undermine that, and the user-agent is device data being turned into stored claims about the user's OS vendor.
- Raised during review of the #220 design note (PR #234, decision D2), which recommends tracking this separately.

**Not verified**
- Whether any export/report path presents these entries as verified detections to third parties.
- Whether the DataFlow UI labels them as heuristic anywhere.

## Options (for decision, not yet chosen)
- A. Stop writing PrivacyAuditService results to the audit log until the service is real.
- B. Keep writing them but carry `detection.method`/`confidence` and label them `heuristic` end to end, including UI.
- C. Replace the mock with only directly observed facts (see #220 design: observed / potential / unknown layers).

## Acceptance
- No audit-log entry is created from mock/heuristic data without an explicit, persisted `heuristic` marker, or none is created at all.
- Regression test in `WalletService.test.ts` covering the chosen behaviour.
EOF

**Why closed**
- **Behaviour change, not a pure optimisation (verified in diff):** `service.ts` now maps unparseable dates to epoch: `Number.isNaN(time) ? 0 : time` (diff lines 95, 116). Invalid `startedAt` values always sort last, and invalid event timestamps always sort first within a group, which changes which event becomes `group[0]`. Corrupt audit timestamps get silently treated as 1970. No test covers it, and the PR doesn't mention it.
- `group.length = 0; group.push(...sortedGroup)` spreads every element as an argument, which can throw `RangeError` on very large groups. The old in-place sort didn't have that risk.
- The "150ms → 100ms" claim has no reproducible evidence. The benchmark printed nothing in a local run, groups are ~5 events, and the work is a micro-optimisation.
- `service.benchmark.test.ts` has no assertions, uses an unseeded `Math.random`, and has an unused `result` variable, but runs in every `pnpm test`.
- A stray `pr_description.md` sits at the repo root.

Tests on the branch tip pass (data-flow: 4 files / 70 tests, after building deps). Not checked: tests merged onto current master.

If the idea is revived: keep master's NaN behaviour or decide and test it explicitly, drop the stray file, move any benchmark to `vitest bench`, and use a plain in-place sort on precomputed keys.

AI-assisted review (2026-11-01, head `3449955`). Entire trail: https://entire.com/gh/late-bloomer420/-/trails/6

**Verdict: fine to merge as a "Proposed" design note after small edits.** Only the one design doc is added. All five #220 guardrails are restated, some more strictly than the issue. No "implemented" wording.

**Please address**
1. **(medium) When are signals collected?** D1 puts a collapsed teaser on the Welcome/Locked cards. If the collector runs on mount, the wallet reads the full set of signals on every lock screen without being asked. Add an invariant: collect only when the panel is expanded, and drop the values on collapse/hide. Also say whether a teaser that's always present fits #220's "not shown on every login".
2. **(low) G2 test is narrower than G2** (lines 24 vs 111). It checks that `visible-signals.ts` imports nothing from `services/`, but not the reverse (nothing except the panel imports it).
3. **(low) G3 test misses one channel** (lines 25 vs 112). The invariant names image beacons, but the spy list has no `Image`/`src` check.
4. **(low) Type doesn't enforce the layers** (lines 26, 102). `{ layer, value?, … }` lets Potential/Unknown items carry a computed `value`. A discriminated union would enforce "nothing in this list is computed".
5. **(low) Copy accuracy.**
   - The reduced UA string freezes the OS version (Windows 11 shows "Windows NT 10.0"), so "your operating system" can be wrong (line 47).
   - `doNotTrack`/`globalPrivacyControl` availability varies by browser (line 54).
   - `permissions.query` for camera/mic/notifications can throw in some browsers, so it needs a per-query try/catch (line 56).
6. **(low) Codebase references.**
   - `mapTrackingPointToIdentityMetadata` is a module-level function in WalletService.ts, not a method (line 94).
   - `readLocalFlag`/`writeLocalFlag` are private to App.tsx, and there is no "clear" helper. "Reopen from Settings" needs a small refactor (line 104).
   - The "mixed-language backlog item" (line 122) couldn't be found. Link it or drop it.

**Confirmed, and worth its own issue (D2):** on master, mock `PrivacyAuditService` heuristics (UA sniffing with fixed confidences) are written to the audit log as `IDENTITY_ACCESS_DETECTED`. `mapTrackingPointToIdentityMetadata` drops `detection.method`/`confidence` (`App.tsx:683` → `WalletService.ts:1853/122`). An issue draft exists and will be filed separately.

Not verified: browser API behaviour wasn't tested live. It's based on the reviewer's knowledge.

AI-assisted review (2026-11-01, head `a0a4a13`) plus Entire findings. Entire trail: https://entire.com/gh/late-bloomer420/-/trails/5

**Verdict: needs changes.** The gap-report correction is right and needed, and the archive copy is byte-identical to the original. But the new "canonical" role map has wrong codebase claims and doubtful legal citations, several copied unchecked from the #235 body.

**Codebase claims (verified)**
- **(high) `REGULATORY_ROLE_MAP.md:56`** says audit trail, consent receipts and disclosure history (`audit-log`, `data-flow`, `evidence`) are "stored on the user's side and under the user's control".
  - `@askmi/evidence` is the CI evidence harness (its package.json: "Security evidence harness … claim→test map, runner, report").
  - Consent receipts live in `wallet-pwa/src/consent-manager/`.
  - §2 itself places AskMI inside the RP boundary.
  - Entire flagged the same contradiction.
- **(medium) `:35`** lists `evidence` as GDPR data-minimisation tooling. It's a test harness.
- **(medium) `:32`** credits "consent receipts" to `connect` etc. `src/packages/connect` has no consent/receipt code.

**Legal citations: likely wrong, please check against EUR-Lex/ETSI (not verified against primary sources)**
- `:32` "eIDAS Art. 6b(6)" looks like the 2021 proposal's numbering. In Reg. (EU) 2024/1183, relying parties are Art. 5b. Entire flagged this too.
- `:42` "Arts. 5a–9a wallet provisions" mixes the two numbering schemes (likely 5a–5f).
- `:46` plus the gap report: "CIR 2024/2983 (verification of qualified attestations)". The reviewer doesn't recognise this number. The Nov-2024 wallet CIRs are 2977/2979/2980/2981/2982.
- `:41` labels CIR 2024/2982 "wallet functionalities". It's protocols and interfaces; 2979 covers integrity and core functionalities.
- `:48` "ETSI TS 119 476" for RP intermediaries. ETSI TR 119 476 is about selective disclosure/ZKP.
- `:26` "no certification regime applies to AskMI" is an unsourced legal conclusion. Suggest "no eIDAS wallet certification regime…, unverified". The CRA and GDPR Art. 25/32 duties may apply.

**Other (Entire + review)**
- The archive copy republishes "fully compliant for LoA High / 53/53 (100%)" with no "historical, not current evidence" banner. The sibling `archive/EUDI_CIR_MATRIX_2026-06-02.md` has one. The link to `EUDI_CIR_MATRIX.md` (line 3) needs `../`.
- "MATURITY_AND_LIMITATIONS.md §3": that file has no numbered sections. Use "Evidence rules, item 3".
- **"Closes #235" overclaims.** A3 (scoping each ✅), A4 (vocabulary sweep: e.g. `docs/vision/STATE_OF_MITCH.md:9` "Production-ready", `docs/_core/07_ROADMAP.md:45`, `ADR-004.md:4,25`) and B (link from MATURITY_AND_LIMITATIONS) are not done. Change to "Refs #235", or finish them.
- The role map calls itself "canonical" but isn't registered in DOCS_CANON. Dated notes have no source SHA.
- The memo body still says "reduces … liability surface to near-zero" under a "CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL MEMORANDUM" title with an unverified named counsel.

Closing after AI-assisted review (2026-11-01, branch tip `3503d5d`, origin/master `002ce5e`). Entire trail: https://entire.com/gh/late-bloomer420/-/trails/14

**Why closed**
- **Behaviour change, not a pure optimisation (verified in diff):** `service.ts` now maps unparseable dates to epoch: `Number.isNaN(time) ? 0 : time` (diff lines 95, 116). Invalid `startedAt` values always sort last, and invalid event timestamps always sort first within a group, which changes which event becomes `group[0]`. Corrupt audit timestamps get silently treated as 1970. No test covers it, and the PR doesn't mention it.

content.text:
I've filed it as **#245**: https://github.com/Late-bloomer420/miTch/issues/245

The issue covers:
- **The path:** the mock `PrivacyAuditService` guesses things from the browser's user-agent string. When the user accepts the privacy modal (`App.tsx:683`), those guesses are written to the audit log as `IDENTITY_ACCESS_DETECTED` (`WalletService.ts:1853` → `:122`). On the way, the fields that mark them as guesses (`detection.method: 'HEURISTIC'` and the confidence value) are dropped.
- **Why it matters:** the audit log is meant to be evidence, and it ends up holding made-up claims about the user's operating system vendor.

! entire configure --skip-push-sessions --project
